newsitem.title: MEXICO: Salomon recommends Mexican corporate bonds.
newsitem.headline: Salomon recommends Mexican corporate bonds.

text.p: Mexican corporate bonds in the seven to 10 year maturity range have been oversold in recent weeks and offer investors a buying opportunity, Salomon Brothers said in a report released on Friday.

"We believe that the Cemex 12.75 percent notes due '06; Televisa 11.875 percent notes due '06; TV Azteca 10.5 percent notes due 07; and Durango 12.625 notes due 03 currently trade at attractive spreads," it said. While political concerns remain acute, the economy continues to grow, which will lead to top-line revenue growth among Mexican companies.

"Spreads in these notes widened between 60 and 70 basis points between March 6 and April 3. Before buying these assets, however, investors may be prudent to continue monitoring the Fed," Salomon said.
"Concerns regarding the drug-related recertification of Mexico and the approach of the July elections have likely added to weakness in this sector," the company said.

It said the Televisa and TV Azteca notes offer investors the greater upside potential. While it believes the yields on Cemex and Durango paper are attractive at current levels, the potencial for capital appreciation of the bonds is limited by the growth oriented strategies of both companies.
